milestones.title: Rename
acceptance_criteria: No source, manifest or deployment file references the old scope

milestones.title: Verify
acceptance_criteria: The workspace installs, builds, type-checks and tests with the new scope

tasks.title: Inventory every reference of the old scope
tasks.objective: List every file that mentions the old scope so the rename tasks cover all of them
tasks.estimate_rationale: A grep over the repository, excluding node_modules and the lockfile, already returned 17 matches in 9 files

complexity.justification: A search with a known pattern; no design choice involved

scope.justification: Read-only inventory, nothing in the repository changes

duration.justification: One grep and a review of 17 lines

risk.justification: Read-only task with no side effects

coupling.justification: Feeds T2 to T4 but changes nothing they touch

confidence.justification: The grep was already run and listed manifests, sources, Dockerfile and netlify.toml

acceptance_criteria: Every file that references @training/ outside node_modules is listed in the task notes
Dockerfile and deployment files are included, not only package manifests

tasks.title: Rename the contracts package and its API consumers
tasks.objective: Make the contracts package and every API file use the new scope while keeping the API buildable
tasks.estimate_rationale: Four manifests/sources plus the API Dockerfile; mechanical, but the package name is a contract of the workspace

complexity.justification: Find and replace of a known string in known files with no semantic decisions

scope.justification: Five files across two workspaces, extensive but uniform

duration.justification: Five small edits plus a lockless typecheck of one workspace

risk.justification: A missed reference breaks installs or the Docker build, found by the build in T5

coupling.justification: Web, root scripts and Netlify all resolve the same package names, so the three rename tasks must be sequenced

confidence.justification: All references in these files came from the grep inventory

acceptance_criteria: API imports and Dockerfile build steps use the new scope

verification.purpose: the API compiles against the renamed contracts package

tasks.title: Rename the web package and its imports
tasks.objective: Make the web workspace and its type imports use the new contracts scope
tasks.estimate_rationale: Two files in apps/web; it only compiles once T2 has renamed the package it imports

complexity.justification: Replace a known string in two files

duration.justification: Two edits and a type check of the web workspace

risk.justification: A wrong import name fails the type check immediately

coupling.justification: It imports the package T2 renames and shares the workspace scope with T4

confidence.justification: Both files are listed in the inventory and are small

acceptance_criteria: apps/web/package.json is named @trainingapp/web and depends on @trainingapp/contracts

verification.purpose: web compiles against the renamed contracts package

tasks.title: Rename root scripts and the Netlify build command
tasks.objective: Update the root npm scripts and the Netlify build command to the new workspace names
tasks.estimate_rationale: Seven script lines in package.json and one command in netlify.toml

complexity.justification: Eight literal replacements in two files

scope.justification: Two configuration files in the repository root

duration.justification: Eight single-line edits and one grep

risk.justification: Netlify build breaks silently if a name is wrong, so T5 builds the whole workspace

coupling.justification: The scripts call the workspaces that T2 and T3 renamed

confidence.justification: Both files were read and every occurrence was in the inventory

acceptance_criteria: Every -w argument in package.json scripts names a renamed workspace

verification.purpose: no old scope remains in these two files (count 0 per file)

tasks.title: Regenerate the lockfile and verify the whole build
tasks.objective: Refresh package-lock.json for the new names and prove the workspace builds and tests
tasks.estimate_rationale: npm install rewrites the lockfile for renamed workspaces; the build and test run dominate the time

complexity.justification: Needs a judgement on how npm rewrites the lockfile for renamed workspaces and what to do if it hoists differently

scope.justification: One generated file changes, validated by the whole build

duration.justification: An install, a three workspace build and the tests; a Next build is the slow part

risk.justification: A lockfile rewrite can change resolved versions unnoticed, so the diff must be reviewed

coupling.justification: Runs after every rename task and nothing else edits the lockfile

evidence: assumption:npm updates workspace names in the lockfile without version drift
confidence.justification: The scripts exist but the install behaviour with renamed workspaces was not tried

acceptance_criteria: npm run build, npm run typecheck and npm test succeed from the root

verification.purpose: contracts, api and web build in order
